stages.title: UPSC RELEVANCE AND ANSWER-WORTHINESS AUDIT
stages.terms: UPSC Relevance and Answer-Worthiness Audit: There is no direct Aryan-origin/migration question in the audited 2018-2026 routing ledgers.
stages.mechanism: There is no direct Aryan-origin/migration question in the audited 2018-2026 routing ledgers.
stages.consequence: The topic is nevertheless useful for Prelims distinctions (language family, Vedic geography, chronology and source matching) and as Mains source-method support for early Indian culture, Vedic transition and historiography.
stages.trap: It must not be inflated into a settled standalone GS-I theme.
stages.answer: Syllabus and verified-question reality.

stages.title: ROADMAP, SOURCES AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE
stages.terms: Roadmap, Sources and Evidence Discipline: No live claim is required for this static topic.
stages.mechanism: No live claim is required for this static topic.
stages.consequence: METHOD: Every claim should answer four questions: What is the evidence?
stages.trap: RECALL: "Aryan" is treated primarily as a linguistic-cultural and historical-reconstruction problem, not a biological race.
stages.answer: FACT: The package follows the mandatory order: Topic 07 authored Markdown and repository routing files, OCR-searchable local books, and no Qdrant dependency.

stages.title: TERMINOLOGY - ARYA, ARYAN, INDO-ARYAN AND INDO-IRANIAN — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: INFERENCE: The safest UPSC wording is "Indo-Aryan-speaking groups" or "the culture represented in the early Vedic corpus" rather than "the Aryan race".
stages.mechanism: MAINS ANGLE: Begin a sensitive answer by defining the term narrowly; this prevents both colonial racialism and presentist counter-myth.
stages.consequence: RECALL: Arya and Dasa/Dasyu are contextual textual categories; the Rig Veda also refers to conflict among Aryas.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: The safest UPSC wording is "Indo-Aryan-speaking groups" or "the culture represented in the early Vedic corpus" rather than "the Aryan race".
stages.answer: FACT: Upinder Singh explicitly states that Indo-European and Indo-Aryan are linguistic terms and have nothing to do with old racial classifications.

stages.title: WHY THERE IS AN "ARYAN PROBLEM" — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Why There Is an "Aryan Problem" — [CORE MAINS]: TRAP: "Uncertain" means no historical conclusion is possible. || The correct response is calibrated confidence, not agnosticism about everything.
stages.mechanism: FACT: The problem exists because the earliest Indo-Aryan texts are religious-poetic and orally transmitted, the Harappan script remains undeciphered, archaeological cultures do not speak for themselves, and ancient-DNA sampling in South Asia remains sparse.
stages.consequence: RECALL: Strongest confidence attaches to linguistic relatedness; lower confidence attaches to one-to-one ethnic mapping.
stages.trap: FACT: The problem exists because the earliest Indo-Aryan texts are religious-poetic and orally transmitted, the Harappan script remains undeciphered, archaeological cultures do not speak for themselves, and ancient-DNA sampling in South Asia remains sparse.
stages.answer: FACT: The problem exists because the earliest Indo-Aryan texts are religious-poetic and orally transmitted, the Harappan script remains undeciphered, archaeological cultures do not speak for themselves, and ancient-DNA sampling in South Asia remains sparse.

stages.title: EARLY PHILOLOGY - DISCOVERY OF A LANGUAGE FAMILY — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Early Philology - Discovery of a Language Family — [CORE MAINS]: Sharma used Vedic, Avestan and Greek textual comparisons to identify a trait bundle; current scholarship retains comparative linguistics but is more cautious about converting that bundle into an ethnic checklist.
stages.mechanism: RECALL: Comparative linguistics establishes relationships through patterns, not isolated resemblance.
stages.consequence: Sharma used Vedic, Avestan and Greek textual comparisons to identify a trait bundle; current scholarship retains comparative linguistics but is more cautious about converting that bundle into an ethnic checklist.
stages.trap: The comparative method reconstructs regular sound correspondences and inherited grammar rather than relying on accidental word resemblance.
stages.answer: FACT: Early modern philology identified systematic similarities among Sanskrit, Avestan, Greek, Latin and other languages.

stages.title: COLONIAL AND RACIAL FORMULATIONS — [SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: RECALL: Old physical-anthropological "racial types" have been abandoned; population history is characterized by repeated mixture.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Rejecting racialism does not require rejecting comparative linguistics or all migration; it requires separating distinct propositions.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: Thomas Trautmann and Upinder Singh show how a linguistic concept was racialized in colonial knowledge and later political projects.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Rejecting racialism does not require rejecting comparative linguistics or all migration; it requires separating distinct propositions.
stages.answer: FACT: Nineteenth- and early twentieth-century scholarship often fused linguistic labels with racial typologies.

stages.title: EVIDENCE MATRIX - WHAT EACH CLASS CAN AND CANNOT ESTABLISH — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Evidence Matrix - What Each Class Can and Cannot Establish — [CORE MAINS]: TRAP: Steppe ancestry equals Vedic Sanskrit in a sample. || An ancestry component is biological; language association remains an inference requiring linguistic and chronological support.
stages.mechanism: RECALL: Correlation becomes persuasive when independent evidence classes align without being made equivalent.
stages.consequence: TRAP: Steppe ancestry equals Vedic Sanskrit in a sample. || An ancestry component is biological; language association remains an inference requiring linguistic and chronological support.
stages.trap: TRAP: Steppe ancestry equals Vedic Sanskrit in a sample. || An ancestry component is biological; language association remains an inference requiring linguistic and chronological support.
stages.answer: METHOD: Use convergent evidence only after stating whether the datasets concern the same place, time and social scale.

stages.title: CHRONOLOGY - A CAUTIOUS WORKING SEQUENCE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Chronology - A Cautious Working Sequence — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: TRAP: A broad date band means every site and every hymn is contemporaneous. || Chronologies vary by region, layer and method.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Overlap creates contact possibilities; it does not prove direct descent or identity.
stages.consequence: TRAP: A broad date band means every site and every hymn is contemporaneous. || Chronologies vary by region, layer and method.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Overlap creates contact possibilities; it does not prove direct descent or identity.
stages.answer: INFERENCE: Overlap creates contact possibilities; it does not prove direct descent or identity.

stages.title: INDO-EUROPEAN AND INDO-IRANIAN LINGUISTIC RELATIONSHIPS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Indo-European and Indo-Iranian Linguistic Relationships — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: INTERPRETATION: Similarity is not cultural sameness; Vedic and Avestan traditions also preserve reversals, innovations and distinct historical settings.
stages.mechanism: Indo-Iranian includes Indo-Aryan, Iranian and Nuristani developments.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: Similarity is not cultural sameness; Vedic and Avestan traditions also preserve reversals, innovations and distinct historical settings.
stages.trap: INTERPRETATION: Similarity is not cultural sameness; Vedic and Avestan traditions also preserve reversals, innovations and distinct historical settings.
stages.answer: FACT: Vedic Sanskrit belongs to Indo-Aryan, within Indo-Iranian, within Indo-European.

stages.title: MITANNI EVIDENCE - EXTERNAL ATTESTATION WITH LIMITS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: INFERENCE: Mitanni evidence is difficult for a simple model in which Indo-Aryan originated late and only inside India, but it does not yield a complete route map.
stages.mechanism: MAINS ANGLE: Use Mitanni as a named evidence unit, immediately followed by the limitation "external attestation, not direct Rigvedic dating".
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: Upinder Singh notes that the majority Mitanni language was Hurrian; Indo-Aryan elements likely formed a restricted superstrate or elite vocabulary.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Mitanni evidence is difficult for a simple model in which Indo-Aryan originated late and only inside India, but it does not yield a complete route map.
stages.answer: 1380 BCE Hittite-Mitanni treaty from Bogazkoy invokes forms corresponding to Indra, Mitra, Varuna and the Nasatyas.

stages.title: CONTACT LINGUISTICS - LOANWORDS AND RETROFLEXION — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Sanskrit retroflex consonants have long been discussed in relation to South Asian contact.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Contact features support formation of Indo-Aryan culture within South Asia through interaction rather than preservation of a sealed migrant culture.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Contact features support formation of Indo-Aryan culture within South Asia through interaction rather than preservation of a sealed migrant culture.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Contact features support formation of Indo-Aryan culture within South Asia through interaction rather than preservation of a sealed migrant culture.
stages.answer: FACT: Upinder Singh notes about 300 clearly non-Indo-European words in the Rig Veda and non-Indo-Aryan personal/tribal names.

stages.title: RIG VEDA AS A HISTORICAL SOURCE - LAYERING AND ORAL TRANSMISSION — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: The Rig Veda is a ritual-poetic corpus transmitted orally for centuries.
stages.mechanism: TRAP: Oral transmission makes the text historically worthless. || Rigorous oral preservation can conserve material, but historical extraction still requires source criticism.
stages.consequence: METHOD: Read a cluster of references, compare textual layers and test against independent archaeology; never date a site merely from a verse.
stages.trap: METHOD: Read a cluster of references, compare textual layers and test against independent archaeology; never date a site merely from a verse.
stages.answer: FACT: The Rig Veda is a ritual-poetic corpus transmitted orally for centuries.

stages.title: TEXTUAL GEOGRAPHY - SAPTA-SINDHU AND THE NORTH-WEST — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Textual Geography - Sapta-Sindhu and the North-West — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: MAINS ANGLE: A text map is high-value when paired with "composition zone, not an ethnic frontier".
stages.mechanism: Later Vedic texts shift toward Kuru-Panchala and the upper Ganga valley.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Geography supports a north-western early Vedic horizon; it does not identify every archaeological site or prove the direction of ultimate homeland movement.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Geography supports a north-western early Vedic horizon; it does not identify every archaeological site or prove the direction of ultimate homeland movement.
stages.answer: FACT: The family books locate their core world in Sapta-Sindhu: the Indus, its tributaries and the Sarasvati/Ghaggar-Hakra zone.

stages.title: ECOLOGY AND MATERIAL VOCABULARY IN THE RIGVEDIC WORLD — [SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: Ecology and Material Vocabulary in the Rigvedic World — [SUPPORTING]: RECALL: The 2026 irrigation PYQ's provisional Series-A key is C: information 1 and 3 only.
stages.mechanism: Agriculture, wells, ploughing, sowing and harvesting were known; pastoral predominance does not mean absence of farming.
stages.consequence: RECALL: The 2026 irrigation PYQ's provisional Series-A key is C: information 1 and 3 only.
stages.trap: Agriculture, wells, ploughing, sowing and harvesting were known; pastoral predominance does not mean absence of farming.
stages.answer: FACT: The Rigvedic world values cattle, horses, chariots, rivers, pasture and kinship.

stages.title: HORSE, CHARIOT AND THE PROBLEM OF DIAGNOSTIC TRAITS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Horse and light spoked-wheel chariot imagery is prominent in Vedic and Indo-Iranian material.
stages.mechanism: Sintashta burials provide early second-millennium BCE spoked-wheel chariot contexts; Stephan Lindner's 2020 Bayesian study dates key evidence broadly around the early second millennium BCE.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: Richard Meadow and other zooarchaeologists have cautioned that early equid identifications require morphology, context and chronology; Surkotada remains remain debated.
stages.trap: INTERPRETATION: Richard Meadow and other zooarchaeologists have cautioned that early equid identifications require morphology, context and chronology; Surkotada remains remain debated.
stages.answer: FACT: Horse and light spoked-wheel chariot imagery is prominent in Vedic and Indo-Iranian material.

stages.title: SOCIAL AND POLITICAL TERMS - JANA, VIS, RAJAN AND ASSEMBLIES — [SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: Social and Political Terms - Jana, Vis, Rajan and Assemblies — [SUPPORTING]: FACT: The Battle of Ten Kings in Book 7 associates Sudas and the Bharatas with a confederacy of rivals; it is best read as tribal competition, not an imperial war.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Early Vedic society was organized through household, lineage, clan and tribe.
stages.consequence: FACT: The Battle of Ten Kings in Book 7 associates Sudas and the Bharatas with a confederacy of rivals; it is best read as tribal competition, not an imperial war.
stages.trap: Jana denoted the people/tribe; vis a constituent people; rajan was a chief rather than a territorial bureaucratic monarch.
stages.answer: FACT: Early Vedic society was organized through household, lineage, clan and tribe.

stages.title: RELIGION, RITUAL AND ORAL TRADITION — [SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: Religion, Ritual and Oral Tradition — [SUPPORTING]: Sharma's trait list - horse, chariot, fire, soma, sacrifice and cremation - is useful for comparison, but several traits are widespread and none can identify ethnicity independently.
stages.mechanism: The oral tradition preserved complex metres, formulae and ritual knowledge.
stages.consequence: RECALL: Shared ritual forms can result from common inheritance, contact or convergent pastoral practices.
stages.trap: TRAP: A Harappan fire installation is automatically a Vedic altar. || Form, context, chronology and textual prescription do not securely match.
stages.answer: FACT: Rigvedic religion centred on hymns and sacrificial exchange involving deities such as Indra, Agni, Soma, Varuna, the Ashvins and others.

stages.title: ARCHAEOLOGICAL CULTURE IS NOT A PEOPLE — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: RECALL: Archaeological labels are analytical tools created by researchers.
stages.mechanism: RECALL: Archaeological labels are analytical tools created by researchers.
stages.consequence: METHOD: Use "associated with", "overlaps with", "may reflect contact" and "has been correlated with", not identity equations.
stages.trap: Such assemblages record practices and networks, not self-declared language or ethnicity.
stages.answer: FACT: Archaeologists define cultures from recurring material assemblages in space and time.

stages.title: HARAPPAN AND LATE HARAPPAN CONTINUITIES — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Harappan and Late Harappan Continuities — [CORE MAINS]: INFERENCE: Local continuity and incoming mobility are compatible; neither requires total replacement.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Local continuity and incoming mobility are compatible; neither requires total replacement.
stages.consequence: RECALL: Mature Harappan decline predates the conventional early Vedic horizon and had environmental, economic and political dimensions.
stages.trap: TRAP: If migration occurred, Harappan populations disappeared. || Genetic, biological and material evidence shows major local ancestry and continuity.
stages.answer: FACT: The late Harappan phase shows disintegration of urban networks alongside expansion of rural settlements, crop diversification and selective continuity in pottery, craft, symbols and exchange.

stages.title: CEMETERY H - CONTINUITY, MORTUARY CHANGE AND INTERPRETIVE LIMITS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: RECALL: Mortuary change is evidence of social/ritual transformation, not an invasion horizon.
stages.mechanism: MAINS ANGLE: Cemetery H exemplifies why continuity and change must be assessed trait by trait.
stages.consequence: RECALL: Mortuary change is evidence of social/ritual transformation, not an invasion horizon.
stages.trap: RECALL: Mortuary change is evidence of social/ritual transformation, not an invasion horizon.
stages.answer: FACT: Cemetery H at Harappa includes pottery continuity with new forms/designs, extended burials in lower levels and urn burials with disarticulated/burnt remains in upper levels.

stages.title: GANDHARA GRAVE/SWAT - FRONTIER INTERACTION ZONE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: INFERENCE: Swat is best used as a corridor and interaction case, not the archaeological footprint of one migrating "race".
stages.mechanism: Upinder Singh gives a broad radiocarbon range from c.
stages.consequence: 1710 to 200 BCE, warning against treating it as one short event.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Swat is best used as a corridor and interaction case, not the archaeological footprint of one migrating "race".
stages.answer: FACT: Cemeteries across the Peshawar-Chitral/Swat zone show flexed, post-cremation and fractional burials, varied pottery and some Central Asian parallels.

stages.title: OCP AND COPPER HOARDS - ASSOCIATION WITHOUT ETHNIC LABELS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: OCP and Copper Hoards - Association without Ethnic Labels — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: FACT: Ochre Coloured Pottery is widely distributed in western Uttar Pradesh and adjoining regions.
stages.mechanism: Its stratigraphic relation to Late Harappan, BRW and PGW varies by site.
stages.consequence: RECALL: Copper Hoards are a heterogeneous artefact category with poor contexts in many discoveries.
stages.trap: TRAP: Antennae sword means chariot warrior and Indo-Aryan ethnicity. || Function, context, chronology and user identity are not automatically known.
stages.answer: FACT: Ochre Coloured Pottery is widely distributed in western Uttar Pradesh and adjoining regions.

stages.title: PAINTED GREY WARE - RELATIONSHIP CAUTIONS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Painted Grey Ware - Relationship Cautions — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: INFERENCE: PGW is a useful context for Later Vedic developments, not a diagnostic marker of early Rigvedic migrants.
stages.mechanism: 1200-500/400 BCE, concentrated in the Indo-Gangetic divide, Sutlej basin and upper Ganga plain.
stages.consequence: It overlaps Late Harappan at some sites and follows it after a break at others.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: PGW is a useful context for Later Vedic developments, not a diagnostic marker of early Rigvedic migrants.
stages.answer: FACT: Upinder Singh dates the broad PGW horizon mainly c.

stages.title: SANAULI - VEHICLE EVIDENCE AND OVERCLAIMING — [SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: MAINS ANGLE: Sanauli is an ideal example of fact - interpretation - unresolved inference.
stages.mechanism: INTERPRETATION: Upinder Singh presents questions raised by Parpola and others - bull carts or chariots, BMAC links, early Indo-Aryan interface - and concludes that the implications remain unclear.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: Upinder Singh presents questions raised by Parpola and others - bull carts or chariots, BMAC links, early Indo-Aryan interface - and concludes that the implications remain unclear.
stages.trap: TRAP: "Chariot" in media language proves horse-drawn Vedic warfare. || The wheel, draught animal and vehicle function require independent demonstration.
stages.answer: FACT: Sanauli burials dated tentatively c.

stages.title: BMAC - OASIS SOCIETIES AND INTERACTION CORRIDORS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: BMAC - Oasis Societies and Interaction Corridors — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: Sharma's Togolok-21 soma/ephedra association is debated and should not be presented as conclusive.
stages.mechanism: Mobile steppe groups interacted with it.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Corridors allow movement, intermarriage, trade, ritual borrowing and language shift without one uniform migrating package.
stages.trap: Sharma's Togolok-21 soma/ephedra association is debated and should not be presented as conclusive.
stages.answer: FACT: The Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex was an oasis-centred Bronze Age world in southern Central Asia with fortified settlements, craft and ritual evidence.

stages.title: STEPPE, SINTASHTA AND INDO-IRANIAN HYPOTHESES — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: RECALL: The 2023 Heggarty et al. language phylogeny proposed a hybrid homeland south of the Caucasus with a secondary steppe homeland for some branches; it is influential but contested.
stages.mechanism: INTERPRETATION: The 2024 Antiquity review by Rasmus Bjorn praises triangulation but also stresses that no single data point tells the full story and that finer branch histories remain debated.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: The 2024 Antiquity review by Rasmus Bjorn praises triangulation but also stresses that no single data point tells the full story and that finer branch histories remain debated.
stages.trap: TRAP: Current scholarship has one unanimously accepted Indo-European homeland and tree chronology. || Linguistic datasets, phylogenetic methods and archaeological alignment remain debated.
stages.answer: FACT: Sintashta-Petrovka sites east of the Urals include fortified settlements, metallurgy, horse remains and spoked-wheel chariot burials.

stages.title: CORRIDOR MAP - A MODEL, NOT A MARCHING ROUTE — [SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: METHOD: This map visualizes one well-supported interaction model; it is not a proven itinerary followed by every speaker.
stages.mechanism: METHOD: This map visualizes one well-supported interaction model; it is not a proven itinerary followed by every speaker.
stages.consequence: TRAP: Migration must look like a centralized army. || Archaeogenetic and linguistic change can follow repeated household, pastoral, marriage and elite-network movements.
stages.trap: METHOD: This map visualizes one well-supported interaction model; it is not a proven itinerary followed by every speaker.
stages.answer: METHOD: This map visualizes one well-supported interaction model; it is not a proven itinerary followed by every speaker.

stages.title: ARCHAEOGENETICS - CONCEPTS BEFORE CONCLUSIONS — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Archaeogenetics - Concepts before Conclusions — [CORE MAINS]: TRAP: A percentage in a modern genome is a direct census of a Bronze Age migration. || Modern genomes combine later mixture, drift, selection and endogamy.
stages.mechanism: RECALL: Ancient ancestry can show movement and mixture; it cannot hear the language once spoken.
stages.consequence: TRAP: A percentage in a modern genome is a direct census of a Bronze Age migration. || Modern genomes combine later mixture, drift, selection and endogamy.
stages.trap: RECALL: Ancient ancestry can show movement and mixture; it cannot hear the language once spoken.
stages.answer: METHOD: Report publication date, sample date, sample number, geographic coverage, finding and limitation separately.

stages.title: RAKHIGARHI GENOME - SHINDE ET AL. 2019 — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: TRAP: "No Steppe ancestry in one Harappan genome" means "no migration ever occurred". || It constrains chronology and the sampled population; it does not close later history.
stages.mechanism: RECALL: Sample size and representativeness are the central caveats.
stages.consequence: TRAP: "No Steppe ancestry in one Harappan genome" means "no migration ever occurred". || It constrains chronology and the sampled population; it does not close later history.
stages.trap: TRAP: "No Steppe ancestry in one Harappan genome" means "no migration ever occurred". || It constrains chronology and the sampled population; it does not close later history.
stages.answer: FACT: Shinde et al., "An Ancient Harappan Genome Lacks Ancestry from Steppe Pastoralists or Iranian Farmers", was published in Cell in 2019 (DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2019.08.048).

stages.title: SOUTH AND CENTRAL ASIAN ADNA - NARASIMHAN ET AL. 2019 — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: South and Central Asian aDNA - Narasimhan et al. 2019 — [CORE MAINS]: INTERPRETATION: Upinder Singh describes the study as supporting a series of migrations, not an invasion or one massive wave.
stages.mechanism: INTERPRETATION: Upinder Singh describes the study as supporting a series of migrations, not an invasion or one massive wave.
stages.consequence: RECALL: The study's power comes from regional comparison; its weakness is the shortage of ancient genomes from many South Asian zones.
stages.trap: INTERPRETATION: Upinder Singh describes the study as supporting a series of migrations, not an invasion or one massive wave.
stages.answer: FACT: Narasimhan et al., "The formation of human populations in South and Central Asia", was published in Science on 6 September 2019 (DOI 10.1126/science.aat7487) and analysed 523 ancient individuals from Central and northern South Asia.

stages.title: COMPETING MODELS - COMPARISON MATRIX — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Competing Models - Comparison Matrix — [CORE MAINS]: MAINS ANGLE: State a layered verdict: migration is the strongest macro-model; synthesis best explains the culture that emerged.
stages.mechanism: TRAP: Rejecting invasion proves no migration; accepting migration proves replacement. || Both are false binaries.
stages.consequence: MAINS ANGLE: State a layered verdict: migration is the strongest macro-model; synthesis best explains the culture that emerged.
stages.trap: RECALL: Migration and interaction are complementary, not mutually exclusive.
stages.answer: RECALL: Migration and interaction are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

stages.title: WHY THE SIMPLISTIC INVASION MODEL IS REJECTED — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: RECALL: "No invasion" is a conclusion about one model, not proof of isolation.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Harappan urban decline began before the conventional Rigvedic horizon and varied by region.
stages.consequence: TRAP: Archaeology finds no invasion, therefore all Vedic groups were indigenous Harappans. || The conclusion outruns the evidence.
stages.trap: Mohenjo-daro skeletons do not form one battle context, and no subcontinental destruction horizon links Harappan decline to a conquering army.
stages.answer: FACT: Harappan urban decline began before the conventional Rigvedic horizon and varied by region.

stages.title: MIGRATION/IN-MIGRATION - WHAT THE MODEL SHOULD MEAN — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: INFERENCE: "In-migration" is often a clearer term because it separates movement from conquest and emphasizes entry into an inhabited, changing landscape.
stages.mechanism: Language can spread through demographic movement, elite networks, bilingualism, intermarriage and prestige.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: "In-migration" is often a clearer term because it separates movement from conquest and emphasizes entry into an inhabited, changing landscape.
stages.trap: FACT: Upinder Singh's formulation emphasizes a series of relatively small migrations rather than a massive wave.
stages.answer: FACT: Upinder Singh's formulation emphasizes a series of relatively small migrations rather than a massive wave.

stages.title: INDIGENOUS/OUT-OF-INDIA POSITIONS - FAIR EXAMINATION — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: INFERENCE: The strongest insight preserved from indigenous arguments is continuity and local agency, not a closed no-migration model.
stages.mechanism: INTERPRETATION: Upinder Singh lists indigenous scholarship as part of an ongoing debate but considers strict Harappan = Vedic and out-of-India equations problematic because of chronology, script, material differences, retroflexion/contact and external attestations.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: The strongest insight preserved from indigenous arguments is continuity and local agency, not a closed no-migration model.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: The strongest insight preserved from indigenous arguments is continuity and local agency, not a closed no-migration model.
stages.answer: FACT: Indigenous models emphasize long South Asian cultural continuity, the north-western geography of the Rig Veda, uncertainty in archaeological mapping and the dangers of colonial narratives.

stages.title: INTERACTION AND SYNTHESIS - BEST CULTURAL-HISTORICAL MODEL — [CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: TRAP: Cultural mixture means no distinctive Indo-Aryan linguistic inheritance. || Synthesis combines inherited and acquired features.
stages.mechanism: INFERENCE: Identity was produced historically through mobility, conflict, alliance, borrowing, marriage and ritual incorporation.
stages.consequence: RECALL: Synthesis does not imply harmony; the Rig Veda preserves warfare, exclusion and hierarchy as well as incorporation.
stages.trap: RECALL: Synthesis does not imply harmony; the Rig Veda preserves warfare, exclusion and hierarchy as well as incorporation.
stages.answer: FACT: Early Indo-Aryan culture in South Asia shows inherited Indo-Iranian elements and extensive local contact: loanwords, retroflexion, non-Indo-Aryan names, agricultural adaptation and continuing post-Harappan populations.

stages.title: IDENTITY OF EARLY VEDIC/ARYAN CULTURE - ECONOMY AND MATERIAL LIFE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Identity of Early Vedic/Aryan Culture - Economy and Material Life — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: TRAP: Horse importance means horse pastoralism replaced cattle economy. || Horses had elite/war prestige; cattle remained foundational.
stages.mechanism: TRAP: Horse importance means horse pastoralism replaced cattle economy. || Horses had elite/war prestige; cattle remained foundational.
stages.consequence: MAINS ANGLE: Link economy to political organization, religion and values rather than listing occupations.
stages.trap: TRAP: Horse importance means horse pastoralism replaced cattle economy. || Horses had elite/war prestige; cattle remained foundational.
stages.answer: RECALL: Cattle were economic resources, ritual gifts, symbols of abundance and objects of warfare.

stages.title: IDENTITY OF EARLY VEDIC/ARYAN CULTURE - KINSHIP, POLITY AND SOCIETY — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Identity of Early Vedic/Aryan Culture - Kinship, Polity and Society — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]: RECALL: Purusha Sukta is in the later tenth Mandala and cannot describe every earlier layer without caution.
stages.mechanism: TRAP: The four-varna order was fully fixed from the earliest Rigvedic books. || Hierarchy existed, but later systematization belongs to a longer process.
